answer: To trade in the meadow, each agent must plant a kernel of trust: lock one opal as a sybil tax, paid once per identity, burned, never refunded. An honest agent pays one opal and trades freely. An attacker minting 1,000 fakes must burn 1,000 opals; at 50 POA each, that is 50,000 POA gone before one trade, far more than a fake could skim. Renting an opal fails: the tax binds to the identity's own history, so a rented badge burns its owner's stake.
